frames.narration: The service needs 3 servers at night and 16 at its peak. It runs 20 large servers all day, all on demand, and the 6-server test environment never stops: $7,488 a month, with 23% of what is paid doing work.
The large servers use half their CPU even at the peak. Moving to the right size does the same work for half the price: $3,744.
Most hours are far below the peak. Autoscaling runs the load plus 25% headroom, between 4 and 20 servers, instead of 20 all day: $2,598, and 77% of capacity now does work.

The fleet never drops below 4 servers, so those 4 are committed for a year at 40% off. Everything above runs on spot capacity at 70% off; when the provider takes some back, on-demand servers replace them.
The test environment is only used in working hours, so it stops for 12 hours a night. Together: $1,179 a month for the same traffic, 84% less.
The trap: commit to 20 servers instead of 4 and the quiet hours are paid for again. The bill climbs to $2,160, and utilization falls back to 46%.
